beer-hagolah/1:א: (א) Mishnah Megillah 31 — as in Pesikta on the 25th of Kislev the work of the Mishkan was completed — Tur
beur-hagra/1:א: (א) Seif 1: And they begin — for the miracle was done through them. Tur:
beur-hagra/1:ד: (ד) And they read the portion — in order to finish with the candles — Tur; see in Pesikta on the portion Beha'alotekha:
biur-halacha/3:א: (א) And if he erred and began, etc., he must stop, etc. — see Mishna Berurah in what we wrote in the name of Taz who disagrees and rules: since he began reading for Hanukkah the kohen must finish this Torah for Hanukkah; in Eliyah Rabbah he sides: if he has not yet read three verses for Hanukkah he stops in the middle and reads for Rosh Chodesh [if he read three verses he agrees with Taz the kohen blesses final blessing and others read for Rosh Chodesh and need not return to Hanukkah reading]; so he sides somewhat in Mor VeKetzia; nevertheless many Acharonim [Bigdei Yesha, Shulchan Shlomo, Penei Yitzchak siman 69, Dagul MeRevavah, Chayei Adam] — from them also Magen Avraham at end siman 140 — ruled like Taz: since he began for Hanukkah the kohen must finish this sefer Torah then read the three in another sefer for Rosh Chodesh (even though in this siman Magen Avraham explained Rama's reason — for halacha certainly his view as written there). Beginning is called from when he began to bless — i.e., began the blessing Baruch Atah; but if he did not begin to bless even though a scroll happened to be ready for Hanukkah — all agree not to be concerned; roll it and read in another scroll brought for Rosh Chodesh — no blemish to this scroll since they will read in it later [Acharonim]. On Rosh Chodesh Tevet falling on Shabbat requiring three scrolls — Hanukkah matters read in the third — as above; if they erred and read the second for Hanukkah and third for Rosh Chodesh — nevertheless read haftarah for Hanukkah because of publicizing the miracle [Chayei Adam]; similarly Peri Megadim sides at end of his words — see there; nevertheless b'dieved if they read Rosh Chodesh haftarah HaShamayim Kisai they fulfilled [there]. One who has Yom Tov Sheni of Hanukkah should not count per Hanukkah days but per month days — sometimes Rosh Chodesh Tevet is day one, sometimes two days.
chatam-sofer/1:_: In Mechaber seif 3 in Hagahah — Rosh Chodesh reading — see siman 140. NB: see what I wrote there on the margin — not like Dagul MeRevavah here.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (ב) There. And they begin with Birkat Kohanim — a fine custom since the miracle was done through kohanim. Tur. Levush. Taz s.k. 2:
machatzit-hashekel/2:ב: (ב) (And so from Tosafot's wording without "Rav Safra said so" — meaning Rav Safra: frequent precedes; impossible the questioner did not know Rosh Chodesh has superiority without the reason Shabbat is frequent — why is Shabbat deferred more than Rosh Chodesh? What superiority of this over that?) Since the first questioner's difficulty was only that they needed two recognitions — even regarding Hanukkah we also do two recognitions for publicizing miracle: one in kindling lights, second in Torah reading; nevertheless one would think specifically for Hanukkah through two recognitions we do not defer frequent; certainly two recognitions are preferable; not so for Rosh Chodesh — through two recognitions need to defer the law that frequent precedes — this was not raised until answered that even so we do two recognitions; per this without "Rav Safra" one would think Shabbat is entirely deferred; one may say the questioner also concluded since deferral is not needed, preferable to defer Shabbat's portion even though it is frequent, because of Rashi's reason to publicize it was established, etc. — for deferral the reason of publicity is preferable to frequent; even though otherwise no publicity and recognition needed — nevertheless for deferral perhaps the questioner concluded we do two recognitions unlike after two "Rav Safra said" for precedence — not so for publicity — one would think we do not do two recognitions anyway; therefore Tosafot hold no difference between deferring or preceding — both equal and in both frequent is preferable — examine. Incidentally I saw in the responsum he left Tosafot and Rosh in requires study per what he wrote — only for deferring publicity is preferable but for preceding frequent is preferable; if so why is Rosh Chodesh before Shabbat — for Rosh Chodesh there is publicity it was established, etc.; nevertheless Shabbat which is frequent should precede — end; in my humble opinion no difficulty: for Hanukkah the reason to precede frequent is because anyway there is publicity only later for lights; but there for Rosh Chodesh no publicity except in what preceded Shabbat; if they had preceded Shabbat's portion it would not be known at all that Rosh Chodesh was established in its time — they would know the day is Rosh Chodesh but still waver as Rashi wrote; by giving it precedence of preceding it is publicized plainly to the court they sanctified it properly as Rashi wrote — obvious in my view.
peri-megadim/3:_: For Rosh Chodesh — ATZ; Tosafot Shabbat 23b d.h. hadar and Rosh there — although two other answers, this is primary as siman 681:1 — see there. Also read Hanukkah haftarah in what he concluded — aside from Simchat Torah haftarah he reads from sacrifices and haftarah in Joshua vayehi acharei, etc. — see Levush 669 and here; what begins on Shabbat day — see siman 325 and Levush; see Peri Chadash where they say mizmor shir chanukat, etc. — on Hanukkah after prayer — shir shel yom: for us one may say previous day's shir since frequent, then Hanukkah shir — requires study.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: (Seif 1) In Shulchan Aruch they read from sacrifices, etc. — see these laws and law of error in reading in my books Shaarei Ephraim gate 8 — all explained well.
turei-zahav/1:א: (א) They read from the Nesi'im offerings. Tur wrote and explains in Pesikta because the Mishkan work was completed on the 25th of Kislev — end. Meaning Moshe erected the Mishkan only on Rosh Chodesh Nisan and then the Nesi'im brought their offering; we read the Nesi'im portion on Hanukkah after completion of the Mishkan.
yad-ephraim/2:_: Taz s.k. 4: he sacrifices for frequent then sacrifices for non-frequent, etc. — to pray Minchah on Shabbat, etc. — so it should read.
turei-zahav/3:ב: (ב) If one erred and began [Chanukah reading before Rosh Chodesh]. So writes Abudraham: from "prevent" it implies that if he left it so he did not fulfill — he must place them in mitzvah order — his view is that for Chanukah and Rosh Chodesh too, if he preceded Chanukah he must return in the order Chazal said. Wondrous! First, this gemara he brings for tefillin is nowhere in the Talmud. Further, Beit Yosef siman 28: if one encountered head-tefillin first he passes over that mitzvah and puts arm-tefillin first; so Rosh and Rambam, unlike Raavad who wrote to put head first without passing over — all agree that if he already put head then arm he need not remove them and replace in order; Shulchan Aruch 25 likewise — not a great novelty that even after head then arm he need not remove; once they are on his head and arm b'dieved he fulfills tefillin — the reason in the gemara: "between your eyes" — while between your eyes let them be two; and so too Chanukah reading before Rosh Chodesh — b'dieved he fulfilled though he transgressed tadir kodem. This is proven in Kol HaTadir (Zevachim 91): if tadir and not-tadir and he preceded and slaughtered the not-tadir — do we say since he slaughtered he offers it, or perhaps he waits for its blood until he offers the tadir and then offers the not-tadir? If you thought that transgressing tadir kodem invalidates even b'dieved, why would the Talmud doubt what to do after this precedence — it would be totally invalid immediately upon transgressing tadir kodem? Rather certainly invalidation does not apply from this. Further proof from Zevachim: minchah prayer precedes musaf because minchah is more tadir; we hold siman 286 that if he preceded musaf prayer to minchah he fulfilled — only l'chatchila minchah comes first. From siman 108: one forgot minchah on Shabbat, prayed twice on Motzei Shabbat, made havdalah on the second not the first — the first did not count since he must pray the obligatory prayer first and must pray a third time — we do not say b'dieved suffices that he changed and prayed the makeup first; there it is different because the makeup prayer has no time at all that hour since he must pray the obligation of his hour — like praying a prayer not in its time; unlike musaf and minchah whose times are both present, only minchah has the advantage of tadir — I wrote this in siman 108. It appears to me that this Rama ruling is not solid reliance; since he opened b'dieved on the Chanukah portion we do not make him return to read Rosh Chodesh first; further there is a dispute whether he must return and bless on what he returns to read as noted siman 140 — how can we say he should stop and begin Rosh Chodesh reading and enter himself into a beracha doubt? Rather the main point is b'dieved the kohen reads the Chanukah portion and afterward others read Rosh Chodesh as above; so too Maharal R' Naphtali Katz in a responsum — only he came to analyze the gemara Abudraham brings; I told him it is not a general rule in the gemara as above and he regretted and said he relied on him thinking it was in the gemara but in truth it is not in the gemara. Written in Maharil responsum 280: once the chazan forgot and read the fourth [aliyah] on "and on your new months" and said Kaddish and read the fourth again the Chanukah portion — he ruled there one need not return and repeat Kaddish after Chanukah reading; what he wrote that the fourth read Chanukah again is already explained in Shulchan Aruch that one must read the fifth on the Chanukah portion.
